fan_analyst.note: The Phillies Show crew is bullish on Wheeler and Duran's talent ceiling but genuinely alarmed by Turner's prolonged slump and the need for a right-handed bat.

radio_populist.note: WIP High Hopes host frames the blown save as a bummer but not a crisis, praises Mattingly's aggressive moves, and is increasingly absorbed in the Skubal-vs.-bat trade deadline debate.

youtube_fan.note: YouTube commenters are split on Duran's historical standing versus Lidge, and angry that the offense can't score enough runs to protect leads.

twitter_fan.note: X posts are dominated by betting recaps and game score reactions; genuine fan sentiment is thin but reflects mild frustration over the blown-save loss and 15 strikeouts.

themes.name: Duran's perfect run ends, but trust holds
themes.sample: The first blown save of the season stings, especially on a pair of infield bleeders, but the consensus is that one bad outing doesn't change what Duran has been all year — and the broader question of a long-term extension is already being debated.

themes.name: Wheeler and Sanchez carry the rotation
themes.sample: The top two starters keep putting up gem after gem — combined 13-3 with a sub-2 ERA — and the feeling is that as long as those two take the ball, the team has a chance every fifth day regardless of what surrounds them.

themes.name: Turner's slump is becoming a real problem
themes.sample: The leadoff hitter looks lost at the plate — working around pitches rather than through them, pull-happy, with no plate coverage — and there's no obvious in-house solution to move him down for.

themes.name: Trade deadline debate intensifies: Skubal or a bat?
themes.sample: The Skubal discussion is pulling fans in two directions — a rotation that already looks historically good versus an offense that still can't consistently score four runs — and a thin farm system makes every option feel expensive.

themes.name: Back-end rotation and Painter remain a liability
themes.sample: Painter's fastball is getting crushed and his command is erratic enough that meaningful in-season improvement feels unlikely; the feeling is that the back of the rotation is something that needs to be either fixed over the winter or addressed at the deadline.

vibe_summary: A gut-punch blown save from an otherwise untouchable closer has turned the conversation toward what this offense still can't do — and whether the deadline answer is a rotation titan or a bat that can actually protect leads.
reasoning: The dominant emotion is the sting of a winnable game lost on unlucky infield hits, but there is no panic about Duran himself. Analytical framing is more measured — the blown save is contextualized as fluky — while raw fan commentary fixates on the offense's chronic inability to put games away and Turner's alarming slump. The deadline debate is already consuming significant bandwidth, with the Skubal-or-a-bat argument pulling sentiment in opposite directions and the farm system's thinness shading every option toward anxiety rather than excitement.
